sections.text: In the destruction of a family, the immemorial religious rites of that family perish; on the destruction of spirituality, impiety, indeed, overcomes the whole family.
When irreligion spreads, the women of the house begin to stray; when they lose their purity, adulteration of the stock follows.
Promiscuity ruins both the family and those who defile it; while the souls of our ancestors droop, through lack of the funeral cakes and ablutions.

We had been discussing Chapter 1, Arjuna Vishada Yoga, the Yoga of Arjunas Grief. So far in Chapter 1, we have seen that Arjuna was very confident before the declaration of war and was anxious to get started. But when he decided to look at the situation in its entirety, he started melting down.
We have seen Arjunas meltdown, overwhelmed by the sheer enormity of the task and its consequences. We work all of our life to achieve something, and then comes a defining moment. That defining moment, how we behave, will determine the outcome of what we achieve in life.
There is a Gujarati saying: Ghora Dasarana Divase Na Doda, the horse who has been preparing all year for the race on Dashera day does very well in practice, but doesnt run on race day. This is a defining moment for Arjuna. They suffered through all the cruelties and injustices, and now came the time to fight against that.
But just looking at the enormity of the task, he realized hes not prepared for it. First, he breaks down in his mental attitude, and then he starts justifying why this task is not for him. His first argument was: By killing our relatives, we are going to incur sin.
There is no good going to come out of this war, because we are fighting against our own people, our own uncles, our own teachers, our own grandparents, and our in-laws. So what is the point? For whom do we desire this kingdom? We work hard in our life for the people in our family. But if those people in our family are standing against each other and they are ready to destroy each other, what is the point in gaining anything? So there was the first argument.
What is the point of fighting this war to get this kingdom? Because for those for whom we are fighting this are ready here to sacrifice their own lives and everything they have on both Sides so he doesnt see really a good outcome. I see bad omen that nothing good is going to come out of it. And then he said, not only that nothing good is going to come out, but killing your own people is a sin.
Even though they are felons, even though they are criminals. So till the time he was seeing the world black and white, there was not much issue. He saw Kauravas as real people and on his side good people, there was not really much problem.
He wanted to go eliminate all the evil in this world. But when he saw that evil is not pure evil and good is not pure good, this is what we face in life. Situations we encounter are not black and white.
They are not cleanly divided between good and bad. Everything in life comes with its own side effects. So any medicine you take is not purely killing the disease, but it will also kill something good in you.
So the decision to take is whether the side effects are more important or curing the disease is more important. You take chemotherapy. Obviously there are side effects, but you have to to persevere the side effects to kill the disease.
So Arjuna is missing that point here. So hes trying to make his argument why this war should not be fought and let those criminals continue doing their criminal acts because they are our relatives. That was his first false argument.
If there are other people not my relatives, I will have no problem getting rid of them. But because they are my relatives, I think its a sin. Even that argument did not make much impression on Krishna.
Because he was looking for Krishnas validation that his argument is correct. We shouldnt be fighting this war. But he comes to the point that he had already made up his mind.
So in verse 37 we have seen that he said tasmat, therefore we shall not fight this war. Hes already made up his mind. Previously he made an argument saying I cant stand, I think Im seeing bad omens.
But now he said, I have made up my mind, I do not want to fight this war and we should not fight. Not only I should not fight, we should not fight this war because there is nothing good is going to come out of it. Killing our people is sin.
That argument did not make any impression on Krishna. So he continued in his argument saying kulakshaye pranashyanti, kuladharmaha sanatanaha. By killing these people we will be killing the family units.
By fighting this war well be killing the head of the family and each family. And once that head of the family is destroyed. The family will be destroyed.
These people on the other side, theyre not realizing this, that this is the greatest sin to destroy families. But at least we are wise enough to realize the value of family unit, and therefore we should not be committing this sin. So what we are seeing here is the social structure at the time.
The family was the unit of the society at the time. And the family was not, as we see family now, always a joint family coming from generation to generation, living together and passing on their values from one generation to another. Theres always an older generation available to give guidance to the next generation and to enforce the values and the discipline on the second generation.
So he said, with that lineage will be broken. The family unit changed it from a joint family to a couple, husband and wife. So this was Phyllis, It was written in 50s and 60s.
In our time now, thats not a family anymore, or thats not the unit of the society anymore. The unit of the society now is an individual, therefore individual rights. What we are more concerned about in our modern time, previously we have seen a couples rights were more important.
And even today we are fighting about who is considered a couple and who gets the inheritance. But in those days, in Arjunas time, the family unit was most important, where not one generation, but generations have lived together with each other and passed on their values. You see, when you destroy that lineage of people living together in a family, there will be disaster in the society because youre destroying the unit of the society.
And whoever is the cause for the destruction will be the greatest sinner. We know the other people are doing that, but they are ignorant people. We are not ignorant people.
Therefore, we shall not engage in the same sinful act. Kulakshaye, Pranashanti, Kula, Dharma, Sanatanah. This eternal Dharma of a family, eternal means because it came from generations, from generations.
My parents did what they were taught from their parents. Their parents did what they were taught from their parents. That lineage is continuing, and I have a responsibility to pass it on to my next generation.
Thats called Eternal Kuladharma, that in our family we only do things this way. Dharme, Naste, Kulam, Krishnam, Dharmo, abhi, Bhavyatut. And if Dharma is destroyed, then the entire order in the society will be there, Krishnam.
Entire the whole society. The Dharma of the whole society will be destroyed. As we have seen in our culture, there is Dharma for everything.
That which makes you what you are is your Dharma. So I as an individual has a Dharma. I as a member of my family has my own Dharma that I can only act this way.
I as a part of the society has Dharma as a part of the civilized society. How I act and behave, the society has its own Dharma. So all these Dharmas which are dependent on an individual and in this case individual family, Arjuna says they will be all destroyed.
The whole society will be in disarray because there is no order. There is no order in the family. Therefore there will not be order in the community.
And there is no order in the community. There is no order in the society. And we will be the guilty parties that we started this war.
And all this happened. So Adharma bhi bhavat Krishna Pradishyanti Kulastriyaha. And hes trying to demonstrate how this Dharma will now be destroyed.
Why war will destroy Dharma in the society. Now none of these arguments is invalid. The argument he is making are all valid argument.
Because we have seen after wars this does happen. And they may have seen that too. However, at that time, the only remedy was the war.
Sometimes the disease is so acute you have to take the side effects with it. But it is more important to kill the disease. Because by fear of the side effects, you dont take the medication, then the disease will kill you.
So here it was very important to cure the disease. But Arjuna is now more focused on the side effects. So hes now explaining to Krishna, saying aaa Dharma bhi bhavat Krishna pradishyanti kulastriya ha.
Because now the society has no order. It will corrupt the women in this society. Now obviously we all get very upset when it comes to this type of statement in our scriptures.
But remember one thing. The context of this statement is society at that time, not the society today. Society today has given enough opportunities for women to be independent.
They can function independently. You dont really need a man to support you. Just two generations ago, that was not really possible.
You remember at least? I remember because Im old enough to remember my older generation, which was relatively living a similar life. So when a daughter is given away, they used to give us three dhan eventually became a dowry. Was not really a dowry in the olden society.
It was given as a security wealth to the woman. If something happens to her husband, she will be protected. She will have means to support herself.
There was called Tridhan in the marriage. The parents of the bride will give it to the bride as a gift. And that is Supposed to be very sacred, that you will not touch, that you will not waste, that Sridhan, the husband will have no right to use this Sridhar.
There was a security for that woman because there was no other means for her to support herself. Now you can regress it back to 3,500 years ago, when society was completely different, where the division of labor was clearly defined between men and women. Our society had evolved from hunter gatherer society.
The hunter gatherer society, there was very clear division of labor. Men will go out and hunt and bring food, women will stay in the caves and take care of children. Obviously you couldnt reverse that in that society.
And that was basically a model continued in our society where men went out and worked in the world outside to generate wealth and women took care of the family. Now, if the man is out, the one part of that unit which was responsible to support the family is gone. And if the woman does not have any means to do that, then obviously there will be corruption.
Arjuna is making his argument here, that why it is so important to keep the family unit intact. So in that time society, maybe one person dies in a family, but there was other male in the. In the family who will be there to take care of the widow and her children.

In these verses, Arjuna makes his most elaborate argument yet, a cascade of social consequences. Verse 40: Kulakshaye pranashyanti kuladharmah sanatanah, when families are destroyed, the ancient family dharmas perish. Verse 41: Adharmabhibhavat.. Pradushyanti kulastriyah, when adharma prevails, women become corrupted. Verse 42: Sankaro narakayaiva, this intermixture leads to hell, and the ancestors fall, deprived of their ritual offerings (pinda and water). Contextualizes this for us: these arent universal truths but reflect the social structure of Arjunas time, when the family (kula) was the fundamental unit of society. Today, that unit has contracted to the couple, and now to the individual. But the underlying concern, that violent disruption creates cascading social breakdown, remains relevant. However, notice what Arjuna is NOT seeing: the Kauravas had ALREADY destroyed the family. Years of attempted murders, cheating at dice, public humiliation of Draupadi, thirteen years of exile, the fabric was already torn. Arjuna speaks as if he has a choice between preserving an intact family and destroying it. But that choice was made long ago, by others. This is crucial for our own lives. When we face difficult decisions, we sometimes imagine were choosing between peace and conflict. But often, by the time we face the choice, the damage is done, by others, by circumstances, by time. Our real choice isnt between ideal outcomes but between facing reality and pretending it doesnt exist. Where in your life are you imagining a pristine option that no longer exists? What family dharma are you trying to preserve that has already been violated by others actions?
